pageCache.pageTitle: Music | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music at The Haven
Music at Haven is vibrant, inclusive, and central to our creative curriculum. Through singing, playing instruments, composing, and listening, children develop musical skills and confidence while exploring sounds from different cultures and historical periods.
Our progressive curriculum builds year-on-year, starting with sound exploration in Reception and culminating in composition and performance in Year 6. Lessons are practical, engaging, and accessible to all learners, with opportunities for whole-class instrumental learning and cross-curricular links.
Music supports personal development, teamwork, and self-expression—helping every child find their voice and enjoy the journey of music-making.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sunrisers & Twilight | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Sunrisers
The school offers a before school club which starts at 7.30am every day located in the Community Room, the children who arrive before 8.10 am are offered breakfast everyday.
A range of activities, games and play opportunities will be offered each day which will help develop concentration, social skills and confidence. The cost of the club is £4.50 per day per child via the schools online payment system Arbor.
The children are then taken to their classes at the start of the school day.
Bookings are made in advance only, via a booking form sent to your email address.
Twilight
The school offers Twilight after school care which starts at 3.15 pm and runs till 6.00 pm each day. The children must bring their own snack and take part in a range of games and opportunity to play and have a chance to develop social skills. Payment is to be made on Arbor, bookings are made in advance only, via a booking form sent to your email address.

pageCache.pageTitle: Young Carers | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Young Carers at The Haven
Young Carers at The Haven
At The Haven, we are committed to supporting the wellbeing of all pupils, including those who are Young Carers. We understand that some children take on responsibilities at home that can impact their emotional, social, and academic lives, and we are here to help.
What is a Young Carer?
A Young Carer is someone aged 18 or under who helps care for a family member due to:
A physical disability
A learning disability
A long-term illness or health condition
A mental health condition
Alcohol or substance misuse
What Might a Young Carer Do?
Young Carers may take on a wide range of responsibilities at home. These can include:
Helping with personal care such as washing, dressing, or feeding
Managing household tasks like cleaning, cooking, or shopping
Supporting with finances, such as paying bills or budgeting
Providing emotional support to a relative experiencing anxiety or depression
Administering medication or assisting with mobility
Some Young Carers may be the main carer, while others share responsibilities with parents, siblings, or extended family.
How We Support Young Carers at The Haven
We recognise the unique challenges Young Carers face and aim to provide a supportive and understanding environment. Our wellbeing provision includes:
A safe space to talk and be heard
Access to our Children’s Wellbeing Support Lead and ELSA
Opportunities to connect with peers in similar situations
Support with managing school life and responsibilities at home
Signposting to external services where needed
We also follow the DCAT Wellbeing Framework, which helps us ensure that all children—including Young Carers—receive consistent, compassionate support across our school community.
If you think your child may be a Young Carer, or if you would like to talk to someone about support, please contact the School Office and ask to speak to:
Miss Gibson – Senior Leadership Team Young Carer Lead
Mrs Gilbert – Young Carer Lead
We are here to listen, support, and work together to ensure every child feels safe, valued, and ready to learn.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art at The Haven
At The Haven, our Art and Design curriculum is rooted in the National Curriculum and designed to inspire creativity, confidence, and self-expression. Pupils explore a wide range of techniques including drawing, painting, sculpture, and mixed media, while learning about artists and cultural traditions from around the world.
Art is taught across three terms each year, with a focus on developing key skills through practical, inclusive, and exploratory lessons. Children use sketchbooks to generate ideas, experiment with materials, and reflect on their progress. A spiral curriculum ensures that skills are revisited and built upon with increasing complexity.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils will:
Create imaginative and purposeful artwork.
Demonstrate proficiency in a range of artistic techniques.
Evaluate and discuss art using subject-specific vocabulary.
Understand the historical and cultural development of art and design.

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Computing at The Haven
At The Haven, Computing is a dynamic and essential part of our curriculum, equipping children with the skills and understanding they need to thrive in a digital world. We aim to develop confident, responsible, and creative users of technology who can apply their knowledge across a range of contexts.
Our curriculum is structured around three key strands:
Computer Science – Children learn how digital systems work and develop their programming skills through logical reasoning, problem-solving, and hands-on coding projects.
Information Technology – Pupils create digital content, analyse and present data, and explore how technology can be used to solve real-world problems.
Digital Literacy – We teach children how to use technology safely and respectfully, with a strong emphasis on online safety, privacy, and responsible behaviour.
Computing is taught weekly across all year groups, using a variety of devices and software to support learning. Each year begins with a focus on online safety, which is revisited regularly to ensure children understand how to navigate the digital world securely and responsibly.
Our curriculum is progressive and inclusive, allowing pupils to build on prior knowledge and develop increasingly sophisticated skills. From creating pictograms and animations in Key Stage 1 to designing games, coding simulations, and exploring artificial intelligence in Key Stage 2, children are encouraged to be curious, collaborative, and resilient.
Computing is closely linked with other subjects such as Maths, Science, Design & Technology, and PSHE, providing meaningful opportunities for cross-curricular learning. We also explore real-world applications of technology, including spreadsheets, databases, blogging, and digital presentations.
We monitor the impact of our Computing curriculum through pupil voice, assessment, and regular subject reviews, ensuring that every child leaves The Haven with the digital skills and understanding needed for the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Years at The Haven
At The Haven School, in our Early Years Foundation Stage we want learning to be fun and imaginative. We know that children come into school with a wide variety of experiences. Therefore, as a result we adapt our curriculum to meet the needs and interests of the children.
Our goal is to develop inquisitive, confident learners who ask questions, problem solve and show resilience in their learning whilst fostering independence. Our children develop a secure foundation with the essential skills, knowledge and attitudes that prepare them for a smooth transition into Year One. Our staff support this through shared experiences as well as positive relationships and partnerships with parents and carers.
We strive to provide good quality teaching and learning in an environment where everyone is nurtured and cared for. We continually promote our school Christian Values of respect, courage, responsibility, justice, compassion and hope. Our school vision ‘Let Your Light Shine,’ embodies these values.
We are committed to providing a curriculum which is broad, balanced and stimulating, enriched with learning experiences and opportunities. We provide opportunities for a mixture of child initiated and adult led learning as well as the direct daily teaching of reading, writing and mathematics.
Our learning environments include two classrooms and an outside classroom. The children can choose the areas that they would like to learn in throughout the day. This facilitates them to play, engage, enquire, discover and reflect as they explore the world around them.
Our children develop a love of learning and are confident learners. Through meaningful interactions and conversations, staff focus on developing language acquisition and expanding the children’s vocabulary. This enables children to use language proficiently and to develop the tools to become effective communicators.
In addition, the children take part in weekly Forest School sessions throughout the whole year. We firmly believe that by engaging with the natural world, children in our early years gain confidence, develop important life skills, and build a strong foundation for lifelong learning and wellbeing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Phonics | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Phonics at The Haven
At The Haven, we use Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised – a highly regarded systematic synthetic phonics programme (SSP) used by many schools across the country.
This programme is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect the latest research, ensuring we deliver the very best practice in phonics teaching.
Why do we use Little Wandle?
We chose Little Wandle because it:
Provides a clear and consistent approach to phonics teaching across the whole school.
Helps children learn to read and spell by recognising the sounds (phonemes) that letters and groups of letters make.
Supports all learners, including those who need extra help, through daily practice and regular assessment.
Builds confidence and fluency in reading from the very start of Reception.
Children are taught phonics every day, beginning in Reception and continuing into Year 1 and beyond if needed.
They learn GPCs (grapheme-phoneme correspondences) – the link between letters and sounds.
They practise reading fully decodable books that match the sounds they’ve been taught.
Regular assessments help us identify children who need extra support, which is provided through targeted interventions.
How can parents help at home?
Read with your child every day – even just 5–10 minutes can make a big difference!
Use the wordless and decodable books sent home to practise the sounds your child has learned in school. These books are first shared in small group sessions at school, so your role at home is to celebrate and build their confidence with a book they already know.
Encourage your child to sound out words when reading or writing.
Look out for phonics workshops and resources we share to support you in helping your child at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Forest School at The Haven
At The Haven, Forest School is a valued part of our curriculum, offering children the chance to learn, explore, and grow in a peaceful, natural environment. Through hands-on experiences outdoors, children develop practical skills, build confidence, and deepen their connection to the world around them.
Why Forest School Matters
Forest School supports children’s wellbeing, creativity, and resilience. It provides:
A calming space that promotes mindfulness and reduces anxiety.
Opportunities to explore, play, and problem-solve in a sensory-rich setting.
A sense of belonging and teamwork through shared outdoor experiences.
A growing awareness of environmental care and responsibility.
Reception pupils attend Forest School sessions weekly, all year round, helping them feel secure and confident as they begin their school journey.
Pupils in Years 1 to 6 take part in a termly block of Forest School sessions across the year, building on their skills and experiences as they progress.
Children learn about fire safety, tool use, seasonal changes, and wildlife, with each year group following a carefully planned progression. Activities include:
Shelter building and knot tying
Cooking over fire and understanding food safety
Using tools safely and creatively
Exploring habitats, life cycles, and natural materials
Sessions are led by a qualified Forest School teacher and supported by additional staff to ensure safety, inclusion, and small group learning.
Forest School helps children:
Build resilience and independence
Develop teamwork and communication skills
Foster curiosity and a love of learning
Strengthen their understanding of the natural world
We regularly review our Forest School curriculum to ensure it meets the needs of our pupils. Pupil voice, staff feedback, and ongoing monitoring help us keep the experience fresh, inclusive, and impactful.

pageCache.pageTitle: Geography | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Geography Curriculum at The Haven
At The Haven, our Geography curriculum is firmly rooted in the National Curriculum for England. It is designed to develop pupils’ knowledge of the world, deepen their understanding of diverse places, people, resources, and natural and human environments, and foster a growing awareness of the Earth’s key physical and human processes.
From the Early Years Foundation Stage through to Year 6, children build a strong foundation in locational and place knowledge, human and physical geography, and geographical skills and fieldwork. Our curriculum follows a spiral structure, ensuring that key concepts are revisited and developed with increasing complexity as pupils progress through the school.
Children are taught to think like geographers—asking questions, using maps and digital tools, collecting and analysing data, and drawing conclusions about the world around them. Enquiry-based learning is at the heart of our approach, with topics such as “What is it like to live in Shanghai?”, “Why are rainforests important to us?”, and “Would you like to live in a desert?” encouraging pupils to explore global issues and local environments.
Fieldwork is a key component of our curriculum. Whether mapping the school grounds in Key Stage 1 or conducting independent investigations in Year 6, pupils apply their learning in real-world contexts. Lessons are inclusive, differentiated, and designed to stretch and support all learners.
By the end of their time at The Haven, pupils will have developed a secure understanding of geographical concepts, a strong sense of place, and the skills to interpret and influence the world around them as informed, responsible citizens.

pageCache.pageTitle: History | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
History at The Haven
At The Haven, our history curriculum is designed to spark curiosity, deepen understanding, and develop critical thinking. Rooted in the national curriculum and enriched by our teachers’ expertise, it offers a rich journey through local, national, and global history. From the Early Years through to Year 6, pupils explore significant events, people, and places, building a secure sense of chronology and a strong grasp of key historical concepts such as power, migration, and change.
Children learn to think like historians—asking questions, analysing evidence, and drawing thoughtful conclusions. Our enquiry-based approach encourages pupils to investigate the past through engaging topics like “How have toys changed?”, “What did the Greeks ever do for us?”, and “What was the impact of World War II on British people?”. Lessons are inclusive, differentiated, and designed to challenge and inspire all learners.
By the time they leave The Haven, our pupils have developed not only a strong foundation in historical knowledge and skills but also empathy, perspective, and a deeper appreciation for the diverse world they live in.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mathematics | The Haven Church of England Methodist Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mathematics at The Haven
At The Haven, we believe that every child is a mathematician. Our maths curriculum is designed to foster curiosity, confidence, and deep understanding from the very start of a child’s learning journey.
Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
In EYFS, children explore mathematical concepts daily through purposeful, play-based experiences both indoors and outdoors. Using the Mastering Number programme as a guide, learning is shaped around children’s interests and current themes, aligned with Development Matters and the Early Learning Goals. Our flexible learning environments encourage children to play, enquire, discover, and reflect—building a strong foundation for future learning.
Language development is central to our approach. Through meaningful interactions, children expand their vocabulary and learn to communicate their mathematical thinking. As they progress, they begin to record their ideas more formally, with increasing complexity throughout the year.
From Year 1 onwards, maths is taught daily using a structured curriculum map based on White Rose Maths. Teachers adapt this curriculum to meet the needs of their class, revisiting concepts when necessary to ensure secure understanding.
Our classrooms are rich in discussion. Children are encouraged to use mathematical vocabulary to explain their thinking, reason effectively, and make connections between concrete, pictorial, and abstract representations. Mistakes and misconceptions are celebrated as valuable learning opportunities.
Independent work is supported by White Rose resources and tailored questioning. Worksheets are used when appropriate, but many lessons focus on hands-on exploration and collaborative dialogue to deepen understanding.
We provide targeted support through small group work, scaffolding, and differentiated outcomes to ensure all children can access the learning. Where needed, bespoke interventions help fill gaps and accelerate progress.
Beyond the Core Curriculum
To build fluency and confidence, our maths provision extends beyond daily lessons. Children benefit from:
Mastering Number (EYFS & KS1) for strong number foundations
Numbots for developing number sense and addition fluency
TT Rockstars to support times tables recall and track progress
Weekly Arithmetic Practice using Rising Stars assessments
Fluent Maths Practice (KS2) tailored to individual needs
Engaging times tables activities including songs, games, and interactive tools
Maths-focused Early Work to revisit key concepts and close gaps
